observations.content: Assistant surveyed pi session lifecycle events: agent_start/agent_end are low-level run boundaries (agent_end fires when run ends but pi may still retry/compact/continue), agent_settled fires only when pi will NOT continue automatically (ctx.isIdle() true, full rest), turn_start/turn_end fire for EVERY turn (one LLM response + tool calls), before_agent_start fires after user submits prompt before agent loop and can inject message + modify system prompt returning {message:{customType,content,display}}, input fires on user input, message_end can replace messages.
Assistant concluded agent_settled fires only at full rest (not mid-run), so the right design for mid-run injection uses turn_end as primary plus before_agent_start plus agent_settled as backstop.
Assistant confirmed pi.sendMessage injects custom messages that participate in LLM context; for durable TUI-only content NOT sent to LLM use appendEntry + registerEntryRenderer per docs.

Assistant proposed revised Design A refined: child side on message_main appends JSON line to a file queue keyed by parent agent id (candidate paths /tmp/paseo-subagent-queue/<parentAgentId>.jsonl or workspace .pi/), returns queued immediately, no daemon call and no status check; parent side extension drains queue on turn_end via pi.sendMessage, on before_agent_start returns {message} injection, on agent_settled final drain; file append atomic-ish with O_APPEND; zero daemon traffic.

Assistant presented to user in Vietnamese: survey table of events concluding combination of turn_end + before_agent_start + agent_settled, noted upstream amosblomqvist/pi-subagents has no 2-way channel (subagent returns text via tool result only, no file handoff), message_main/message_subagent were additions when porting to Paseo, queue file is persistent and lossless, old polling removed entirely; asked if design is okay or to check queue file placement / dedup when 3 events drain together.

User agreed turn_end/before_agent_start/agent_settled sounds reasonable and asked why the original ext author's video mentions 2-way interaction between agent and subagent, and asked how the ext currently sends messages from main agent to subagent and on which event type, recalling from previous session it is like stop agent then prompt and start again rather than the 3 suggested events.

Assistant read current code: sendToSubagent in paseo-channel.ts:159-163 makes single call send_agent_prompt {agentId, prompt, background:true, notifyOnFinish:true} with no status check, no queue, no poll; comment lines 5-16 state MAIN→CHILD is fire-and-forget with daemon interrupt-and-replaces a busy child (urgency over continuity) while CHILD→MAIN never interrupts and queues until idle (continuity over urgency, mirroring pi native followUp queue).

Web search found amosblomqvist has two separate extensions: pi-subagents (one-shot, ported here as subagent-types, no 2-way) and interactive-subagents in pi-config (spawns in tmux panes, steered and resumed by name, fork of HazAT/pi-interactive-subagents, 2-way with orchestrator sending follow-ups and steering in real time, subagents have ask_question tool).

Web search found author videos: Simple Pi Subagents at youtube KRVYUkM16hE and Pi to Pi: Two-Way Agent Orchestration with the Pi Coding Agent at youtube PIdETjcXNIk; author X post describes subagent interactivity two ways between me and subagents and between orchestrator and subagents.

Assistant explained to user: the video's 2-way interaction comes from the different interactive-subagents extension (tmux-based), not pi-subagents ported here; the 2-way channel in this workspace was self-designed during the port (code comment design agreed with the user); main→subagent today is daemon send_agent_prompt fire-and-forget with interrupt+replace when busy since pi lacks steerActiveTurn (abort current turn + rerun with new prompt), matching user's memory, and it does NOT have the child→main poll bug; proposed symmetric file-queue with 3-event drain for main→child too plus opt-in interrupt:true flag keeping daemon path only for urgent cases, and asked user to confirm.

User asked: so is this a wrong-scope result ('làm nhầm scope'), and asked to evaluate whether any other tool/skill/extension is wrongly scoped similarly due to duplicate names or duplicate functionality.
